summary: QBR + operational health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents last quarter, and roadmap alignment for upcoming Dedicated/private deployment. Customer is evaluating moving larger workloads from hosted to dedicated capacity to reduce unit cost; security and audit requirements (SOC2, KMS) are gating timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we've got about 60 minutes. quick intros?
[00:10] Dana (HelioWorks): Hi all, Dana here, head of ML, Evan and Sasha also on from infra.
[00:15] Evan (HelioWorks): Evan, platform eng.
[00:18] Sasha (HelioWorks): Sasha, CTO
hi.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. Priya and Marcus from our side
Priya's gonna run through performance numbers, Marcus is your CSM so he'll cover ops.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): hey, quick note, transcript may slur some acronyms, sorry, we'll try to call out metrics.
[00:34] Marcus (Redwood CSM): Hi everyone.

[00:45] Jordan: Ok, agenda 
 usage & cost overview, reliability incidents last 90 days, roadmap ask and dedicated/private options, then next steps. sound good?
[00:52] Dana: Yep.

[01:05] Priya: So first, usage. Over Q2 we saw a 42% increase in token volume driven by two new customer support automations you launched in May. The top 3 pipelines are chat-assist, rerank for search, and an embeddings batch job. Chat's average context length is 1.2k tokens, but rerank is short at 120 tokens.
[01:35] Evan: That's right. The batch embeddings run is nightly and accounts for about 28% of tokens but low peak concurrency.

[01:50] Priya: Cost-wise, primary drivers are the chat pipeline due to high prompt+response sizes and repeated cold-start latency inflations. We recommend three lever changes: increase prefix caching for chat, enable continuous batching on the rerank route, and evaluate int8 quantized variant for embeddings to drop GPU memory and cost.
[02:18] Dana: Does prefix caching change anything for correctness? we've seen occasionally stale pre-prompts.
[02:25] Priya: Good question. Prefix caching is safe for static system prompts; if you mutate system context dynamically you need cache invalidation. For user-specific dynamic context we'd recommend per-session KV cache TTL of 10-15 minutes, that keeps correctness but saves ~20% token compute on median.

[02:50] Jordan: On the cost side do you have an estimate of savings if they go dedicated?
[02:55] Priya: Rough ballpark
based on your current mix and using our reserved capacity profiles, you could see 30-45% unit cost reduction at your committed levels, but it depends on utilization and burst patterns. We'll send a model with assumptions.

[03:22] Sasha: One of our main concerns is reliability
last month we had two 5-10 minute blips where latency spiked on the hosted endpoints and that impacted SLAs. what happened?
[03:32] Marcus: I pulled the incident logs
both were during cross-region routing changes and a model variant fallback that caused cold KV warming. We have a mitigation path: sticky routing, pre-warm policies for critical routes, and can pin a canary model for release windows.
[03:50] Evan: Can we get a report that ties incident timeline to which model variant and which region?
[03:56] Marcus: Yep i'll put that in the artifacts. expect a CSV and a short incident writeup.

[04:10] Priya: Also for the spike, the KV cache miss rate rose because of TTLs misaligned to your session patterns. Adjusting TTLs reduced P99 by ~120ms in our test.

[04:30] Dana: Security: we're preparing for SOC2 and need to understand KMS integration, audit logs retention, and VPC connectors for private deployment.
[04:38] Marcus: We have SOC2 artifacts and an ISO pack
i'll share. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM providers; you can bring your key, we rotate per policy. Audit logs are available with configurable retention; longer retention is an add-on. For VPC/private, we have a Private control plane that seats in your VPC or on-prem option; there's a setup checklist.
[05:05] Sasha: How long to stand up a private deployment?
[05:08] Priya: Typically 6-8 weeks for a VPC-hosted private deployment if networking & KMS approvals are timely. On-prem can be 10-12 weeks. We can scope a pilot subset earlier, like just customer-sensitive routes.

[05:25] Jordan: Timeline question
what's your target to move heavier production traffic to dedicated/private?
[05:30] Dana: Looking at calendar, we want to pilot dedicated capacity in Q3 and aim for full migration by end of Q3 or early Q4, depending on security sign-off.

[05:40] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We'll pair a benchmark
24h steady-state + synthetic spikes to validate latency SLOs and cost per token. We'll need a representative sample dataset and traffic pattern.
[05:54] Evan: I'll provision a reduced dataset and low-risk credentials for the bench.

[06:05] Jordan: Great. On the roadmap, you asked about newer model variants for lower-latency throughput
our product team is validating quantization profiles and kernel selections that look promising. For embeddings specifically, switching to int8 on that family reduces memory and improves throughput.
[06:23] Dana: Any quality delta when using int8?
[06:26] Priya: Very minor for embeddings
cosine similarity drift is small; we'll run your sample to validate. For chat models we usually recommend mixed-precision testing first.

[06:40] Sasha: We also have procurement constraints
quote needs to include SLAs, support tier, and terms for data residency. can you reflect that in the proposal?
[06:50] Jordan: Yes, we'll include dedicated SLA, support 24x7 pager for P1s, and data residency options.

[07:02] Marcus: quick ops note
we recommend enabling tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns for top 10 routes to help optimize. that will help you find candidates for caching and batching.
[07:14] Dana: ok yes that would help.

[07:25] Priya: i want to call out one perf caveat
when you run large concurrent rerank batches the CPU-GPU pipeline can saturate on our standard kernel on older GPU families; for that we recommend either a higher instance class or scheduled batch windows. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.

[07:48] Evan: For burst patterns, do you support autoscale bursts on dedicated?
[07:52] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; you can set burst pool size and cost caps. the economics change but you get stable tail latency.

[08:08] Sasha: Another question
do you have any partners for data residency in EU region? We need a region in Germany ideally.
[08:15] Marcus: We have region coverage via our cloud partners in Frankfurt and we can provision private control plane there. i'll include region notes.

[08:26] Dana: on evaluation criteria
our success metrics will be P99 latency under 600ms for chat, cost per 1k tokens under $0.40 average post-dedicated, and zero P1 incidents for scheduled batches.
[08:38] Jordan: noted. We'll include these as acceptance criteria in the pilot doc.

[08:45] Priya: ok quick demo of the cost dashboard (screen share described): showing tokens by route, top cost drivers. chat is 52% of spend, embeddings 28%. with batching and quantization we estimate 18-33% reduction without dedicated, and up to 45% with committed reserved capacity.

[09:20] Evan: Those percent ranges are a bit wide
can you model a middle-case?
[09:25] Priya: yes middle-case will be in the spreadsheet we send.

[09:32] Jordan: any blockers from your procurement side, Sasha?
[09:36] Sasha: mainly need legal to see standard enterprise terms and indemnity; timeline's aligned if contracts are ready by mid-August.

[09:45] Marcus: we'll push enterprise T&Cs and an initial SOW draft along with pricing.

[09:55] Dana: also, we had one-off concern about token logging for PII. do you have redaction options?
[09:59] Marcus: we support token-level redaction on ingest and retention policies; if you need advanced PII scrubbing we can run a short eval of scrubbing pipeline.

[10:12] Priya: last technical note
for the benchmark we'll recommend a mix: 70% chat-pattern traffic, 20% rerank, 10% batch embeddings, and two synthetic 10m spike windows to test autoscale.

[10:26] Evan: ack, i'll try to provision traffic pattern and creds by Monday.

[10:34] Jordan: Recap: Jordan sends pricing and dedicated proposal, Priya runs 24h benchmark, Marcus shares SOC2/ISO and incident CSV, Evan provisions dataset, Sasha/Purchasing will review T&Cs.

[10:50] Sasha: sounds good. any follow-up meeting?

[10:55] Jordan: let's plan a technical deep dive week of July 13th for private deployment and security ops. i'll send invites.

[11:05] Marcus: action items noted in the notes, will follow up in CRM.

[11:15] Dana: thanks everyone.

[11:18] Jordan: thanks all, bye.

[11:21] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mislabels and filler words; timestamps approximate. Attachments referenced: cost-dashboard.pdf (link), dedicated-proposal-draft.docx (link), SOC2-pack.zip (link), incident-report-2026-06.csv (link).
